title: Files that ship or are stored but need not be
headline: The files the repo stores are lean (102 MB tracked, all 150 files in public/ referenced, pictures and fonts stored once); the waste is in what every server function carries and in what a browser is sent, and none of it rests on a feature being unused. sharp's native library (19.8 MB) is in 742 of 832 route traces and the taxonomy (13.3 MB) in 831, 33 MB of the median trace's 52.6 MB, and sharp loads at each cold start of the proxy (35 to 57 ms, 22.5 MB) though no shopper's page draws with it. Four small fixes go first (P0): search thumbnails of uploaded photographs answer 400 today (measured on the built app), font files are not kept by the CDN, the build's page worker runs with source maps on at 4.7 MB of heap per MB of code it loads (+498 MB for 107 MB, measured) on a build that already ran out of its 8 GB once, and nothing reports what a function carries. The completeness check added two: on 3x phones and Retina laptops every product tile downloads the 1600 px file because nothing is kept between 480 and 1600 px (measured in Chromium), and videos, 3D models and theme photographs are stored with a one-hour or five-minute cache where pictures get a year.

clean: public/: all 150 files are referenced (second check, by name). Nothing dead.

Pictures: each upload is two files made in the browser, stored once under a random name with a one-year cache (/home/user/kaizen-store/src/server/media.ts:80). Nothing is resized on the server per request; sharp's 43 calls are all inside functions for jobs, imports and admin or AI tools (every call site read in this pass: all are in async functions).
Chromium (70.1 MB) is traced only into the routes that launch it and is loaded by dynamic import (/home/user/kaizen-store/src/server/browser.ts:11-15); a test holds the list.

The taxonomy's loader is lazy: each file is read once per instance, only when a product has a standard category or a listing has attribute facets (/home/user/kaizen-store/src/server/product-taxonomy.ts:40-52). A store that does not use standard categories pays nothing at run time.
Fonts: files are named by content hash with a one-year immutable browser cache; the stylesheet is kept a year at the CDN. 5.7 MB in Postgres is small. The one gap is AS-9.

Share pictures (og.png) are fallbacks and are kept a day at the CDN with a week of stale-while-revalidate (/home/user/kaizen-store/src/lib/share-card.tsx:30). Review pictures are kept five minutes on purpose: a picture can be withdrawn (/home/user/kaizen-store/src/app/api/reviews/picture/[id]/route.ts:26).

findings.title: The image library (sharp, 19.8 MB) is in 742 of 832 route traces and the proxy's, and loads when the proxy or a route as plain as robots.txt starts
findings.evidence: Twelve server modules import sharp at the top of the file; rg finds 43 calls in them, and I read each: every one is inside an async function, none at module top level. The proxy reaches seven of the twelve by static imports (graph re-run: proxy.ts:11 -> house-switch.ts -> pages.ts -> visibility.ts -> customers.ts -> privacy-erasure.ts -> data-jobs.ts -> api-uploads.ts -> ai-pictures.ts is the shortest chain). In the finished build 742 of 832 traces list libvips (19.81 MB each; trace script re-run), the proxy's trace is 47.9 MB. The second check loaded the built proxy bundle and the robots.txt route in bare node and found libvips-cpp.so and sharp's addon mapped into the process once their async modules settled. My runs: the proxy bundle takes 0.92 to 1.00 s and +197 MB RSS; sharp alone 50 to 57 ms and 22.1 to 22.7 MB at load 2.8 (35 to 41 ms at low load in the second check). No storefront page draws with sharp.
findings.cost: At start: 35 to 57 ms and 22.5 MB RSS to load it, about 4% of the proxy's 0.9 s start and 11% of its 196 MB. On disk: 19.8 MB in 742 of 832 traces (38% of the storefront home's 51.9 MB, 41% of the proxy's 47.9 MB); Vercel packs routes into fewer functions than there are traces, so the copies are fewer than 742.
findings.who_pays: Every visitor whose request meets a cold instance (the proxy runs before every storefront and site page, prerendered ones too), and the server in memory per instance. A store that never makes or edits a picture pays the same. Cold instances come with every deploy and every extra instance at a peak, so this stays after opening.
fix_steps: 1. New file src/server/sharp.ts: import "server-only"; import type sharp from "sharp"; export type { Sharp, OverlayOptions } from "sharp"; export function loadSharp() that keeps one promise of (await import("sharp")).default and returns it, as src/server/browser.ts does for Chromium.

2. In the twelve modules, replace the value import with import { loadSharp } from "./sharp" (plus type Sharp in ai-pictures.ts and theme-shot-files.ts, type OverlayOptions in theme-highlights.ts) and add const sharp = await loadSharp(); as the first line of each function that calls it: ai-picture-marks.ts markFile; ai-pictures.ts shrinkPicture and testPicture; ai-vision.ts challengePicture; brand-marks.ts png; content-packs.ts storeArtPicture; page-looks.ts forModel; picture-editor.ts editLibraryPicture; product-import.ts pictureToLibrary; replicate-images.ts rasterOf, previewJpeg, stretch, pairImage, slices, pictureKind and asPng; replicate.ts stepOpen and the crop helper inside startBackdrops; theme-highlights.ts backdrop, shadow, screen, encode, devices, collage and closeup; theme-shot-files.ts fitted, cut and pictureIsBlank. All are async already, so no signature changes.

3. eslint.config.mjs: a block for src/**/*.{ts,tsx} (ignoring src/server/sharp.ts and test files) with @typescript-eslint/no-restricted-imports naming sharp, allowTypeImports true, and a message that points to loadSharp(). This is the first rule of code review step 4.1.

4. Check on the build: load .next/server/middleware.js and .next/server/app/robots.txt/route.js in bare node, await their exports and read /proc/self/maps (the review's script work/assets/load-proxy3.cjs; make it scripts/trace-sizes.mjs --cold from AS-3). libvips must not be mapped.

5. Later, with the import cycle work (server-graph SG-1 and SG-2, tests-ci TC-2): once src/proxy.ts and the storefront entries no longer reach the twelve modules, sharp leaves their traces (19.8 MB each). AS-3's count of traces with sharp (742) is the number to drive down.

findings.title: The product taxonomy (13.3 MB of JSON) is traced into every route, the proxy and the health check included
findings.evidence: next.config.ts:69 traces src/data/product-taxonomy/* into the key "/**"; its comment gives the reason (the editor, imports, listings, feeds and the AI manager's tools all read it). Re-run: 831 of 832 traces list it, 13.28 MB each; /api/health's trace is 16.2 MB, of which 13.3 MB is the taxonomy. The loader is lazy (product-taxonomy.ts:40-52). By static imports 740 of 828 entries reach the loader (graph re-run), the proxy among them through redirect-resolve.ts:19 -> catalog.ts, so narrowing the key today frees 88 entries, and they are the smallest traces.
findings.cost: 13.3 MB (4.1 MB zipped) in every trace. Its effect on cold-start time was not measured: Vercel packs routes into shared functions and zips them. When read: 21 ms and 11.3 MB of heap for the structure, 8 to 10 ms and 4.7 to 6.5 MB per language, once per instance (second check).
findings.who_pays: The server: the size of every function. No store pays at run time for a taxonomy it does not use.
fix_steps: 1. Now: nothing. Keep the lazy loader and the files, and let AS-3's report show the count (831).

2. When the import cycle is cut (server-graph SG-1) and the entries that cannot reach src/server/product-taxonomy.ts are many more than today's 88: first add a scan test built like src/lib/chromium-trace.test.ts on the shared import walker of AS-3: every page.tsx and route.ts whose static or dynamic imports reach product-taxonomy.ts must match a key in next.config.ts that lists src/data/product-taxonomy/*.

3. Then replace "/**" at next.config.ts:69 with globs for the route families that still reach the loader (the admin's store routes, the storefront's product and listing pages, feeds, the Admin API, the crons that run imports and feeds), and keep the comment's reason.
4. Read the new count from scripts/trace-sizes.mjs and lower its budget.
tests_and_rules: The comment at next.config.ts:67-68 is the written reason; the scan test keeps it true route by route.
src/lib/chromium-trace.test.ts is the pattern.
Tests of the loader (src/server/product-taxonomy*.test.ts, src/lib/product-taxonomy.test.ts) are not touched.
findings.done_when: scripts/trace-sizes.mjs reports the taxonomy in fewer than 831 traces, and the scan test passes: every entry that can reach product-taxonomy.ts is covered by a key.
findings.saving: 13.3 MB per trace that can never read it: about 90 today, more once the cycle is cut. Nothing at run time: it is already lazy.
findings.risk: A route left out of the globs fails in production with a missing file the first time it reads the taxonomy, so the scan test must exist before the key narrows.
findings.notes: P3 because its cost on anything a person feels is unmeasured, the saving today is in the 90 smallest traces, and it depends on the boundary work. Not worth doing: compressing the files on disk (9.2 MB less per trace, but a gunzip per read and no change to the zipped upload), or moving them into Postgres (the read is already once per instance). The run-time side (a shopper's product page with a standard category parses three files, about 40 ms and 22.6 MB once per instance) is functions FN-8; if that is planned, save the category's path and Google id with the product when the owner saves it, so a shopper's function never opens the files. Same as server-graph SG-13.

findings.title: Nothing checks what a server function carries or what the proxy imports
findings.evidence: The browser's scripts have an import walk and byte budgets. The server side has only the Chromium list: no test, script or CI step reads a .nft.json, and nothing limits what src/proxy.ts may import (second check; I re-ran its graph: the proxy reaches 1,309 of 4,126 source files, and still 1,309 with the two cache-tag imports cut). The review's own scripts sum all 832 traces by route and by package in 1.7 s. That report is how I found, in this pass, that four routes carry every file of public/ (5.6 MB) because content-packs.ts:112 reads a file under public by a computed path: harmless, and invisible without the report.
findings.cost: No direct cost. It is why 33 MB of the median trace's 52.6 MB is two assets most routes never use, why the proxy loads 13 MB of code before every page, and why nothing stops the next one.
findings.who_pays: Every visitor (cold starts of the proxy and of pages) and the build, later.

findings.title: Search suggestions ask Next's image service for uploaded pictures and get a 400, so real stores will show empty thumbnails; the service itself is open and unused
findings.evidence: Ten next/image tags; nine carry unoptimized, as picture-sizes.ts:6 says they must; the one in the search box does not (re-counted with rg). Stored pictures have absolute Supabase Storage addresses (media.ts:93); next.config.ts has no images key, and the build's manifest shows remotePatterns [] and unoptimized false. Measured on the built app in this pass: /_next/image?url=<a Supabase Storage picture address>&w=48&q=75 answers 400 with '"url" parameter is not allowed'. The same endpoint with /demo/themes/orbit/stars.webp and w=64 answers 200 with an image: the resizing service is live although no picture is meant to use it. Next leaves .svg sources alone (get-img-props.js:245) and the demo products' pictures are SVG files, so neither the e2e search test nor the team's demo stores show the fault. With images.unoptimized set, Next treats every Image as unoptimized (get-img-props.js:242) and answers /_next/image with 404 (next-server.js:193).
findings.cost: One failed request per suggested product with an uploaded picture, up to six each time the list is drawn (search.ts:376), and an empty thumbnail. On Vercel an open /_next/image is also a billed transformation per distinct file, width and quality; only the 150 files of public/ can be asked for, so that exposure is small.
findings.who_pays: A shopper's browser and Vercel's image endpoint, in every store whose products have uploaded photographs: every real store, from its first day.
fix_steps: 1. next.config.ts: add images: { unoptimized: true } to nextConfig, beside poweredByHeader. Every Image is then served as stored, the search box included, and /_next/image answers 404.
2. src/components/search-box.tsx:144: add unoptimized to the tag, as the other nine have, so the tag is right whatever the config says.

3. A ten-line unit test beside src/lib/chromium-trace.test.ts that reads next.config.ts and expects the text images: { unoptimized: true }, with the reason in its comment (pictures are never resized on the server, D336).

4. e2e/search.spec.ts, in 'a shopper searches from the header': give the demo mug a picture row whose address ends in .webp (insert into commerce.product_media as e2e/performance.spec.ts:100 inserts a media row), type 'kera', and expect the option's img src not to start with /_next/image.
5. docs/performance.md, under the rules: 'Pictures are never resized on the server: images.unoptimized is on, so /_next/image does not exist.'

findings.title: Flags are downloaded even while the switcher hides them, public files have no cache lifetime, and six flags and two textures are far bigger than their job
findings.evidence:
1. The switcher draws an per language's flag in its list and its menu (language-links.tsx:72) with no loading attribute; flags are off by default (language-switch.test.ts:14) and hidden with display:none (part-css.ts:706). Measured in headless Chromium 153: an image hidden with display:none, on itself or a parent, or inside a closed
, is fetched at page load; with loading=lazy it is not, and it is fetched when the
opens. 2. The built app answers /flags/no.svg and /demo/themes/botanica/paper.webp with 'Cache-Control: public, max-age=0' (curl -I), as Next's guide says; next.config.ts adds no cache rule. 3. Six flags are 165 of the folder's 176 KB (es 88.9 KB, hr 40.4 KB; 39.8 KB together as brotli); they are drawn at 20 by 15 pixels. As 60 by 45 pixel WebP files they are 0.3 to 0.8 KB each, 3.0 KB together (made in memory with sharp). 4. Four signature themes' stylesheets load six files from public/: Botanica's 512 px paper tile is 114 KB and its 900 px sprig, drawn at 260 CSS pixels, 65 KB; Atelier's paper 67 KB. Re-encoded in memory: Botanica's paper 34 KB at 256 px, its sprig 26 KB at 520 px, Atelier's paper 18 KB at 256 px; a lower quality at the same size saves little (114 to 98 KB) because paper grain does not compress.
findings.cost: Per full page load (first view, reload, new tab; not an in-site navigation): one request per language's flag, shown or not, and one conditional request per public file already held. Up to 13 KB per heavy flag on a first view, and 179 KB of decoration on a first view of a Botanica store.
findings.who_pays: A shopper's browser, in every store with more than one language and every store on a signature theme. It grows with shoppers.
fix_steps: 1. src/components/language-links.tsx:72: add loading="lazy" to the flag . A hidden flag is then never fetched; one in a closed menu is fetched when the menu opens.

2. next.config.ts headers(): add { source: "/:folder(flags|demo|kaizen)/:path*", headers: [{ key: "Cache-Control", value: "public, max-age=86400" }] }. Next's own server sets its default only when no Cache-Control is set yet (next/dist/compiled/send/index.js checks getHeader first), and Vercel applies configured headers to static files. Keep the rule as a small exported constant in src/lib/csp.ts beside baseRouteHeaders() so a unit test can hold it.

3. Flags: make public/flags/{es,hr,mt,li,pt,cy}.webp at 60 by 45 pixels from the SVGs (a one-off with sharp), delete those six SVGs, and let flagOf() in src/lib/language-flags.ts answer .webp for those six countries. Show the owner the switcher before and after at 1x and 3x.

4. Theme backgrounds: in scripts/theme-art/botanica.js draw sprig at 520 px, and try paper at 256 px there and in scripts/theme-art/atelier.js; run node scripts/theme-art.mjs botanica paper sprig (and atelier paper); show the owner each home page before and after and keep only what looks the same.
tests_and_rules: src/lib/language-switch.test.ts:83-86 (a file for every flag it names): read both extensions.
src/lib/language-switch.test.ts:72-77 (flagOf's answers): none of the six heavy flags is asserted today.
e2e/language-switcher.spec.ts:93 (a shown flag is visible): a lazy image keeps its box, so it passes.
src/lib/csp.test.ts if the header rule lives in csp.ts; one e2e request for /flags/no.svg expecting max-age=86400.
public/flags/LICENSE.txt stays (MIT; derived files are allowed).
docs/signature-themes.md: art is drawn from recipes in scripts/theme-art, so the recipe changes, not the file by hand.
findings.done_when: On a store page with the Languages part and flags off, the browser's request log has no request under /flags/ (one per language today); curl -sI /flags/no.svg shows max-age=86400; du -cb public/flags/* is under 20 KB (176 KB today).
findings.saving: Step 1: one request per language per full page load in a store that does not show flags (most are 0.2 KB; Spanish and Croatian 13 KB each). Step 2: estimate of two to six conditional requests less per repeat load within a day. Step 3: 13 KB per Spanish or Croatian flag on a first view. Step 4: estimate of 119 KB on Botanica's first view and 49 KB on Atelier's, if the smaller tiles pass the owner's eye.

findings.title: The font file route does not tell the CDN to keep the file, unlike the stylesheet route beside it

The second check could not say whether Vercel keeps a function's answer on max-age alone. Vercel's CDN guide answers it: 'To cache the response of Functions on Vercel's CDN, you must include Cache-Control headers with any of the following directives: s-maxage=N ...'. So as written, each browser that does not hold the file reaches the function and Postgres. Not observed in production (no production access in this review).
findings.cost: One function call and one read of about 35 KB of bytea (5.7 MB in 163 files) per font file for every visitor whose browser does not hold it yet: one to a few files per store per new visitor. Not counted in production's statistics, which show no shoppers yet.
findings.who_pays: The server per request and the database, growing with new visitors once the platform opens. A returning browser keeps the file for a year either way.

findings.title: The build's page worker runs with source maps on: about 4.7 MB of heap per MB of server code it loads, and 704 MB of maps written that no function carries
findings.evidence: The second check counted 704 MB of .map files beside 205 MB of server chunks and none in any trace; I re-counted both. New in this pass, the mechanism: Next makes its one static worker (it collects page data and renders the static pages) with enableSourceMaps: config.enablePrerenderSourceMaps (build/index.js:396-408), and that starts the worker with --enable-source-maps (lib/worker.js:71). The build's settings show enablePrerenderSourceMaps true and no source map setting in next.config.ts. Node then reads the map of every chunk the worker loads. I loaded built entries in one bare node process with and without the flag: 142 entries (1,452 chunks, 106.6 MB of chunk JS): heap 290 MB without, 788 MB with; RSS 372 against 921 MB; 2.9 s against 5.1 s. 43 entries (70.5 MB): heap 214 against 543 MB. The proxy's bundle alone (13.2 MB): heap 78 against 133 MB, three runs each. That is about 4.7 MB of heap per MB of chunk each time. docs/build-memory.md says a worker holds 1.3 to 1.9 GB, the margin under Vercel's 8 GB is about 0.8 GB, and on 11 November a build was killed for memory while collecting page data with one worker. Next's memory guide names switching source maps off as a lever; build-memory.md's list of what was tried does not mention them.
findings.cost: On Vercel's build: several hundred MB of the page worker's memory (estimate: up to about 960 MB if it loads all 205 MB of chunks, by the measured ratio; not measured in a build), about 2 s more per 100 MB of chunks loaded, and 704 MB written to disk per build.
findings.who_pays: The build on Vercel's 8 GB machine. A build that runs out of memory fails the deploy for every store, and every push to main is a deploy.
fix_steps: 1. next.config.ts, in nextConfig: add ...(ON_VERCEL ? { enablePrerenderSourceMaps: false } : {}). It is a top-level key, not under experimental. CI's builds and local builds keep their maps.

2. Measure it as docs/build-memory.md did: the build with VERCEL=1 under an 8 GB cgroup cap, sampled per process, before and after. Add both peaks as rows of the table in docs/build-memory.md and name the setting under 'What changed'.

3. A second run by the same method: add turbopackSourceMaps: false to the ON_VERCEL part of experimental (next.config.ts:82). Expect no .map under .next/server (find .next/server -name '*.map' | wc -l prints 0; 704 MB less written). Keep it only if the compile's peak (5.8 GB today) or the build's time falls; record the result either way.
4. docs/audits/code-review-2026-11.md: note the result under step 1.8 in the Progress table and its change log.
tests_and_rules: next.config.ts:34-39: 'Each setting that reads this was measured under an 8 GB cap (docs/build-memory.md)': the new settings must be measured the same way before they stay.
docs/build-memory.md: the lists under 'What changed' and 'Watch'.
No test, script or CI step reads a source map (rg over src, e2e, scripts and .github). scripts/await-deploy.mjs and scripts/next-build.mjs are not affected.
CLAUDE.md, Commands: the sentence on Vercel's build (one worker, no Turbopack cache) gains 'no source maps' if the setting stays.
findings.done_when: docs/build-memory.md's table has a row for each of the two settings with the build's peak under the 8 GB cap, and the kept setting's peak is below today's 7.2 GB.
findings.saving: Not yet measured in a build. Measured mechanism: 4.7 MB of heap per MB of server code a worker loads (+498 MB for 107 MB of chunks). If step 3 stays: 704 MB less written per build.
findings.risk: An error thrown while prerendering on Vercel would show positions in built chunks, not source lines; the same commit's CI build still shows source lines. Production stack traces do not change: no function carries a map today. Both settings are Vercel-only and one line to undo.
findings.already_tracked: Partly: code review step 1.8 'Give the build room' (FH10), Open. It does not name source maps.
findings.notes: The second check filed this as an unmeasured experiment with low confidence. I measured the mechanism and raised it: the build is at its limit, the change is one line and safe, and a failed deploy is the dearest failure here. The build-wide numbers still need the capped run. If Vercel's Enhanced machine (16 GB) is chosen instead, this still shortens the build.

findings.title: Videos, 3D models and theme photographs are stored with a one-hour or five-minute cache, though their addresses never change; pictures get a year
findings.evidence: Added by the completeness check. Pictures are uploaded by the server with cacheControl "31536000" (media.ts:80). Videos, 3D models and custom-field files go from the owner's browser straight to Storage with uploadToSignedUrl(path, token, file, { contentType }): no cacheControl, so supabase-js sends its default "3600" (storage-js index.mjs:598-599 and 1620). Each goes to a new random path (media.ts:192, 217, 309), so the file never changes under its address. uploadBytes() stores with "300" (media.ts:258): theme photographs (theme-shots.ts:252; a unit's files are written, then it is marked done, and a failed try removes them, 264-298) and the videos the page replicator copies to a random path (replicate-assets.ts:82-83). Supabase's guide says the browser's lifetime is this option ('You can still control how long assets are stored in the browser using the cacheControl option', default one hour), while its Smart CDN (Pro plan and above) keeps the file at the edge whatever it says. docs/media-compression.md:51 states the intent for pictures only: kept for a year under their address.
findings.cost: Not measured. After an hour (a background video, a product video, a 3D model) or five minutes (a theme photograph, a copied video) a returning visitor's browser must ask Storage again before it may reuse the file: one round trip per file. On a plan without Smart CDN the edge also fetches the file from the origin again (videos up to 50 MB, models up to 20 MB). Which plan production is on was not checked.
findings.who_pays: A shopper's browser in stores that use videos or 3D models; owners and visitors browsing the theme store; Supabase egress where Smart CDN is not on.
fix_steps: 1. Add cacheControl: "31536000" to the options of uploadToSignedUrl at src/components/admin/video-upload.tsx:129, src/components/admin/media-compress.ts:62, src/components/admin/product-media-tools.tsx:220 and src/components/admin/field-file-upload.ts:27. Each path is new and random.

2. src/server/media.ts uploadBytes() (line 247): a fifth argument keep: "year" | "short", default "short" (300, as today). Pass "year" from src/server/replicate-assets.ts:83 and from src/server/theme-shots.ts:252. Leave the replicator's work pictures (src/server/replicate-store.ts:322, one path per job that is written again) at 300.

findings.done_when: rg -n 'uploadToSignedUrl\(' src/components shows cacheControl on all 9 calls (0 today), and a video uploaded on a test store answers cache-control: max-age=31536000 from Storage (curl -sI on its public address).
findings.saving: Not measured: one round trip to Storage less per video, model or theme photograph each time a visitor returns after its lifetime; origin fetches at the edge where Smart CDN is not on.
findings.risk: A file kept for a year cannot be replaced under the same address: none of these paths is written twice (random names; a finished theme unit's files are never written again). A deleted file stays in browsers that hold it until their copy ends, as with pictures today.
findings.notes: Small per visitor, but the lifetime is fixed when a file is uploaded, so it is cheapest before real owners upload videos: do steps 1 and 2 before opening even though the saving is modest.
